title: Encode the zero-warning bar in workspace lints
description:
The zero-warning and no-unsafe bars move from the gate script and crate-root attributes into the Cargo manifests, so a bare `cargo clippy` reproduces them.

## Background

No `[lints]` or `[workspace.lints]` table exists in `Cargo.toml`, `crates/jit/Cargo.toml` or `crates/server/Cargo.toml`, and the repository has no `clippy.toml`. The bar exists only as `-D warnings` inside `scripts/cargo-ci.sh`. `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` sits on four roots (`crates/jit/src/lib.rs`, `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, `crates/server/src/lib.rs`, `crates/server/src/main.rs`), so integration-test crates are not covered. A scratch-crate probe showed `[lints.rust] warnings = "deny"` makes `cargo clippy` fail on clippy warn-level lints and makes plain `cargo build`/`cargo test` fail on rustc warnings, so no separate clippy group is needed. The MSRV (1.97) supports workspace lint inheritance.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The root `Cargo.toml` declares `[workspace.lints.rust]` with `warnings = "deny"` and `unsafe_code = "deny"`, and both `crates/jit/Cargo.toml` and `crates/server/Cargo.toml` declare `[lints] workspace = true`.
- [hard] REQ-02: No `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` attribute remains in `crates/`, and prose that cites that attribute as the enforcement mechanism (`AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, the comment in `crates/server/Cargo.toml`) names the workspace lint table instead.
- [hard] REQ-03: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` with no extra flags exits zero on the tree and non-zero when any target, integration tests included, introduces a warning.

## Notes

GitHub CI runs clippy with `--all-features`, unlike the gate; aligning the two is out of scope. Existing local `#[allow(...)]` attributes keep working. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

planning.outcome: [workspace.lints] denies warnings and unsafe_code, both crates inherit it, and the per-root #![deny(unsafe_code)] attributes are gone

terminal.test_boundary: a bare cargo clippy run over the workspace
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three manifest edits plus deleting four attributes and sweeping three prose mentions; one config change verified by one command.

title: Compile the integration harness once in jit's test-support surface
description:
The shared in-process integration harness moves from a per-target `#[path]` include into `jit`'s existing `test-support` library surface, so it compiles once.

## Background

`crates/jit/tests/common/harness.rs` (about 336 lines, `#![allow(dead_code)]` because each includer uses a subset) is pulled in by `#[path = "../common/harness.rs"] mod harness;` in four of the ten integration targets: `fast_docs_templates`, `fast_issue`, `fast_rules` and `cli_query_graph` (which uses only `seed_memory_issue`). Each target recompiles it. Everything it needs is already reachable through the `test-support` feature: `commands::test_helpers::memory_executor`, `test_mode::enable` and the public `InMemoryStorage` constructors. `crates/jit/Cargo.toml` enables `test-support` for every test build through its self dev-dependency, so code gated `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))` is compiled once in the library build that every target links. `dev/TESTING.md` documents the `#[path]` convention.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The harness is a module of the `jit` library gated on `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`, beside the existing fixture homes, and carries no blanket `allow(dead_code)`.
- [hard] REQ-02: No integration target declares a `#[path]` include of the harness, `crates/jit/tests/common/` no longer exists, and the four former includers reach the harness through `jit::` paths.
- [hard] REQ-03: The integration-target count is unchanged and the four suites pass with their existing assertions.
- [hard] REQ-04: `dev/TESTING.md` describes the harness at its new library location, with no remaining instruction to `#[path]`-include it.

## Notes

A new `jit-test-support` crate was rejected because it adds a build unit without adding a capability. The build-footprint budgets are re-measured when the epic closes. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

title: Move the error classifier into output::failure
description:
The error classifier moves from the binary into the library as `jit::output::failure::classify`, so every consumer, the HTTP server included, can share one classification.

## Background

`error_to_error_code` (about 353 lines) and `error_to_exit_code` sit at the top of `crates/jit/src/main.rs`. They downcast about forty typed errors (`errors::*`, `commands::*`, `repository_state::*`, `storage::*`, `GraphError`, `io::Error`, `toml`/`serde_json` errors) and walk `error.chain()` for some; the order is semantic (lock timeout first, batch rejection first, `io::Error` before not-found downcasts, ambiguous id before invalid prefix). The vocabulary they produce (`ErrorCode`, `ExitCode`, `JsonError`, `ErrorDetail`) and the fragment `refine_id_error` already live in `crates/jit/src/output.rs`. Three in-binary test modules own the classifier's behaviour: `exit_code_projection_tests`, `repository_state_classifier_tests` and `lock_timeout_classification_tests`. `errors.rs` is the wrong home because `domain/` imports it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs`, declared from `crates/jit/src/output.rs` as the `failure` submodule (the crate's non-`mod.rs` layout, as `gate_presets.rs` with `gate_presets/`), exposes `pub fn classify(error: &anyhow::Error) -> JsonError`; `output.rs` stays the module root.
- [hard] REQ-02: `classify` returns, for every error, the code `error_to_error_code` returns today, preserving its downcast order, and the failure's exit code is `ErrorCode::exit_code` of that code.
- [hard] REQ-03: `error_to_error_code` and `error_to_exit_code` no longer exist in `main.rs`; every former caller in `main.rs` calls `classify`.
- [hard] REQ-04: The three classifier test modules live in `output/failure.rs` as its owning unit tests and pass with their existing assertions; CLI exit-code suites pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-05: No prose in `crates/` or `docs/` names `error_to_error_code` or `error_to_exit_code` or places the classifier or its tests in `main.rs` (including `crates/jit/src/schema.rs`, `errors.rs`, `commands/template_expand.rs` and `commands/issue.rs`), and the generated `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` is regenerated.

## Notes

Details and suggestions that call sites build today are not yet derived by `classify`. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

title: MCP bridge injects --json from the schema's global options
description:
The MCP bridge requests machine output only from leaves that declare their own `json` flag, so it would silently receive human output once `--json` becomes one global CLI flag. This makes the injection follow the schema's `global_options` as well.

## Background

`buildCliArgs(cmdPath, args, cmdDef)` in `mcp-server/lib/cli-executor.js` computes `hasJsonFlag` from `cmdDef.flags` and appends `--json` only when it is true. `mcp-server/lib/tool-generator.js` turns every leaf flag into a tool input property, which is why `json` is a tool property today. The CLI schema printed by `jit --schema` lists globally accepted flags once in `global_options` (today `quiet`, `schema`, `help`, `version`) and keeps them out of each leaf's `flags`. The CLI is moving `--json` to a single `global = true` flag on `Cli`; after that no leaf carries `json`. Supporting both shapes lets the bridge keep working across the cutover.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `buildCliArgs` appends exactly one `--json` when the leaf declares a `json` flag or the schema's `global_options` declares `json`, and appends none when neither does.
- [hard] REQ-02: A global `json` option adds no `json` input property to generated tools, while leaf flags still map to tool properties as before.
- [hard] REQ-03: Unit tests in `mcp-server/test-unit.js` exercise injection against a schema with per-leaf `json` flags and against one with only a global `json` option, and the existing injection and no-duplication tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

How `global_options` reaches `buildCliArgs` (an argument or state held by the executor) is an implementation choice.

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.

planning.outcome: The MCP bridge adds --json when the schema declares it per leaf or globally, without exposing a global json tool property

terminal.test_boundary: mcp-server unit tests of buildCliArgs
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One JavaScript predicate and its caller change in one module, verified by a handful of unit tests against two schema fragments.

title: Wrong-verb hints come only from the parser-level path
description:
Thirteen hidden clap stubs duplicate the wrong-verb hint table and keep the parser-level hint from firing. Deleting them leaves one hint path that needs no argv scan.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/cli.rs` declares 13 `#[command(hide = true, trailing_var_arg = true)]` stubs: `IssueCommands::{Rm, Remove, Complete, Edit}`, `DepCommands::{Remove, Delete}`, `GateCommands::{Rm, Delete}`, `DocCommands::{Rm, Delete}` and `LabelCommands::{Add, Rm, Remove}`. Their arms in `run()` call `verb_hint_error` (`crates/jit/src/main.rs`), which scans the captured arguments for `--json` and returns the hint as an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` error. Dispatch runs after repository validation, so a stub invoked outside a repository reports `REPOSITORY_NOT_FOUND` instead of its hint. Because the stubs claim those verbs, `unknown_subcommand_hint`, which looks the verb up in `COMMAND_HINTS`, prints `Hint: ...` to stderr before clap's error and exits 2, serves only `("invariant", "list")` today. `mcp-server/curated-tools.json` excludes each stub as an "Alias stub", and `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/verb_hint_tests.rs` asserts the hint inside the `--json` failure envelope.

The contract this establishes: clap parse failures, including a wrong-verb guess, stay outside the failure envelope. A wrong verb prints its hint and clap's diagnostic on stderr and exits 2, with or without `--json`. Recovering `--json` after a failed parse would need an argv scan, which the single global output flag forbids, and clap yields no partial matches.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `cli.rs` declares no verb-hint stub, and `main.rs` contains no `verb_hint_error` and no arm dispatching to it.
- [hard] REQ-02: Invoking any `COMMAND_HINTS` wrong verb prints that entry's hint and clap's diagnostic on stderr, writes nothing to stdout and exits 2, with and without `--json` and inside or outside a repository; `verb_hint_tests.rs` states this contract in place of the JSON-envelope hint assertions.
- [hard] REQ-03: `mcp-server/curated-tools.json` names no removed stub, and the MCP curation coverage test passes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Apart from the replaced wrong-verb envelope assertions, the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

The hidden `validate --divergence` flag is not a verb stub and is out of scope.

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.

planning.outcome: The 13 hidden verb stubs are gone and COMMAND_HINTS is served by unknown_subcommand_hint on stderr with exit 2

terminal.test_boundary: CLI integration tests of wrong-verb invocations
terminal.worker_sized_reason: A deletion of 13 declarations, one helper and their arms plus one rewritten table-driven test; no new mechanism is introduced.

title: One global --json flag carried as OutputMode
description:
`--json` is declared 108 times and recovered from raw argv when an error leaves `run()`. This declares it once and threads the parsed mode to every consumer, including failure rendering.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/cli.rs` declares a `json: bool` field on every real leaf and on the bare `Commands::Query` parent; `Cli.quiet` is already `global = true`. Each arm of `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` extracts its own `json` and builds `OutputContext::new(quiet, json)`. `emit_top_level_json_error` scans `std::env::args()` for `--json` because an error propagated from `run()`, including repository discovery, `invocation_write_override` and `storage.validate()` failures raised before any arm runs, no longer carries the parsed flag. `reject_parent_query_filters` treats a parent-level `--json` as a misplaced filter, so `jit query --json available` exits 2 today. `graph export --json` reads the same field as export-format sugar. In tests, `reflected_json_arm_paths_from` in `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_probe_coverage_tests.rs` derives the failure census from schema leaves whose `flags` contain `json`, and `test_schema_has_json_flags` in `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/schema_tests.rs` pins the per-command flags.

The shape: `Cli` declares `#[arg(long, global = true)] json` beside `quiet`; `OutputMode { json, quiet }` in the output module is built once from the parsed `Cli` and is the only source of the flag for arms and for failure rendering; `run()` hands the mode back to `main()` with its result.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `Cli` declares `--json` once with `global = true`, and no subcommand in `cli.rs` declares a `json` field.
- [hard] REQ-02: `OutputMode { json, quiet }` is built once from the parsed `Cli`, `run()` returns it with its result, and `emit_top_level_json_error` reads that mode; no code in `crates/jit/src` reads raw argv for `--json`.
- [hard] REQ-03: `--json` is accepted after any command segment, and a test asserts that `jit query --json available` now succeeds with the list envelope where it exited 2 before.
- [hard] REQ-04: The schema lists `json` once in `global_options` and in no leaf's `flags`; `test_schema_has_json_flags` asserts that global form, and the failure-probe census derives its arm set from executable leaves while still covering every arm it covered before.
- [hard] REQ-05: Human output, success payloads and exit codes are otherwise unchanged, and the Rust and MCP suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

This is a mechanical sweep across every arm of `run()`; it changes no arm's behavior beyond where the flag is read. 2d10f1dd, 3754095f, 16d63038, 8673dc5e and f37d228e edit arms in the same file and land first.

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.

planning.outcome: --json is declared once on Cli and threaded as OutputMode from parse to failure rendering, with no per-command json field or argv scan

terminal.test_boundary: CLI integration tests of the global flag form
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One mechanical substitution repeated per arm with a single new type; the sweep cannot be split because a subcommand field named json collides with the propagated global argument of the same id.

title: Issue lifecycle methods behind an issues facade
description:
Introduces the executor facade shape and moves the issue-lifecycle methods onto it, so an issue consumer depends on `IssueOps<'_, S>` instead of the whole `CommandExecutor` surface.

## Background

`CommandExecutor` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`) carries every command family in one public surface of about 195 methods across 28 `impl` blocks, so a consumer of one family accepts all of them. This family lives in `commands/issue.rs`: `create_issue`, `list_issues`, `show_issue`, `get_dependencies_enriched`, `issue_status_response`, `issue_children`, `issue_progress`, `update_issue`, `update_issue_resolved`, `confirm_deletion_allowed`, `delete_issue`, `update_issue_state`, `assign_issue`, `claim_issue`, `unassign_issue`, `release_issue`, `claim_next`, and the single reject operation if present (`create_issue` carries an extra `RepositoryStateStore` where-clause). Callers: the issue arms of `crates/jit/src/main.rs` (or their handler module under `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`), the server's `list_issues` and `show_issue` routes and its test setup (`crates/server/src/lib.rs`, `routes.rs`, `crates/server/tests/`), other families inside `commands/` (`breakdown.rs`, `document.rs`, `gate_check.rs`, `graph.rs`, `query.rs`, `validate.rs`), `validation/repository.rs`, `crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs`, `commands/test_helpers.rs`, and most integration tests (`create_issue` alone has about 390 call sites in about 50 files, a mechanical rewrite the compiler enumerates).

The facade shape: `CommandExecutor::<family>()` returns a borrowing struct holding `&CommandExecutor<S>`; the family's methods live in `impl` blocks on that struct in the family's own `commands/` file, and each block keeps the storage bound its `impl CommandExecutor` block had (`IssueStore`, `IssueStore + RepositoryStateStore`, or concrete `JsonFileStorage`). The kernel (sessions, rule and config caches, `require_active_lease`, the validation `capture_*` helpers) stays on `CommandExecutor`; a facade method reaches it through its executor reference, and calls into another family go through that family's accessor.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `CommandExecutor::issues()` returns `IssueOps<'_, S>`, re-exported from `jit::commands`, and every public method listed in the Background is a method of `IssueOps` rather than of `CommandExecutor`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each `IssueOps` impl block for these methods carries the storage bound of the `CommandExecutor` block it replaces, so no method becomes callable on a storage it could not use before.
- [hard] REQ-03: Callers in `crates/jit`, `crates/server` and their test suites reach the moved methods through `issues()`, intra-doc links name the new paths, and the workspace builds, lints and passes its existing suites with no assertion changed.

## Notes

- Behaviour, output and exit codes are unchanged; the compile and the existing suites are the test boundary.
- Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md` (D-1); method inventory: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md` area 3.

planning.outcome: CommandExecutor::issues() returns IssueOps carrying the issue-lifecycle methods, establishing the facade shape the other families reuse

terminal.test_boundary: the existing workspace test suites
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One accessor and one file's impl blocks; the large call-site count is a single compiler-driven textual rewrite (`executor.m(` to `executor.issues().m(`) with no judgement per site.

title: Library-side command handler contract
description:
Command bodies live in the binary's `run()`, where the schema cannot see their response types. This establishes the library-side handler contract every command group migrates onto.

## Background

`run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` matches over every command group, and each arm builds its payload, picks its error code, prints and often calls `std::process::exit`. The extracted helpers `run_item`, `run_invariant`, `run_project` and `run_query_all` are still binary-side. `CommandSchema::generate()` (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs`) lives in the library and takes success schemas from the hand-kept match table in `get_output_schema_for_command`, which falls back to `CommandResponse` for 74 of 120 leaves. Handlers must therefore live in the library so that the schema can reach each handler's response type. The building blocks exist: `OutputMode { json, quiet }`, `jit::output::failure::classify(&anyhow::Error) -> JsonError` and `ListEnvelope<K, T, E>` in the output module.

The contract: `crates/jit/src/dispatch/` holds one module per command group. A handler takes its parsed arguments and a `CommandContext` carrying the executor and the `OutputMode`, and returns `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>` where `R` is its registered response type. `Outcome` is either a success or a findings result carrying an `ErrorCode` and a report: under `--json` findings render as the failure envelope with that code as the exit status and the report as `error.details`; in human mode the report prints and the process exits with the same code. Every response is a type owned by the output module, or built by an output constructor wrapping a command-layer result, and derives `JsonSchema` plus a human rendering. One registration per group generates both its dispatch and the schema's per-leaf response lookup, so they cannot drift. Until every group has migrated, schema generation consults the registry first and the legacy table second.

- [hard] REQ-02: One per-group registration generates both the group's dispatch function and its per-leaf response-schema lookup from a single list of leaf, handler and response type.
- [hard] REQ-03: One emitter in the output module renders an `Outcome`: success through the success envelope or the response's human rendering, findings through the failure envelope or the printed report; it returns the exit status and never calls `std::process::exit`.
- [hard] REQ-04: `CommandSchema::generate()` takes a registered leaf's success schema from the registry and any other leaf's from `get_output_schema_for_command`'s legacy table, which stays reachable from the derivation.
- [hard] REQ-05: The layer description in `AGENTS.md` names `dispatch/` as part of the CLI layer that owns dispatch, and states that `commands/` does not import it.
- [hard] REQ-06: Unit tests drive a test-only handler group through registration, dispatch, schema lookup and both outcome renderings, and the generated schema and CLI output of every real command are unchanged.

title: Keep stderr empty for --json failures
description:
Under `--json` a propagated failure renders once, as the stdout envelope, instead of also printing an `Error:` line to stderr.

## Background

`main()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` handles `run()`'s error with `eprintln!("Error: {}", e)` unconditionally and then calls `emit_top_level_json_error`, so every propagated failure under `--json` prints both a stderr diagnostic and the stdout envelope (reproduced with `jit apply plan <id> --json`). Handler-owned failures already leave stderr empty. `test_propagated_config_parse_failure_emits_registered_envelope_and_human_diagnostic` in `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/top_level_failure_envelope_tests.rs` asserts the duplicate stderr line, and `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` says errors are "always shown to stderr". With `--json` declared once as a global flag, the parsed output mode reaches `main()` beside `run()`'s result, so `main()` can choose one rendering.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Once clap has accepted the arguments, a failing invocation with `--json` writes exactly one failure envelope to stdout and nothing to stderr, for propagated and handler-owned failures alike.
- [hard] REQ-02: A failing invocation without `--json` writes one `Error:` diagnostic to stderr and nothing to stdout.
- [hard] REQ-03: The propagated-failure test in `top_level_failure_envelope_tests.rs` states the new contract (empty stderr under `--json`), and a human-mode test owns the single-diagnostic property.
- [hard] REQ-04: The "always shown to stderr" statement in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` describes the new behaviour.
- [hard] REQ-05: `main()` chooses the rendering from the parsed output mode; no raw-argv scan decides it.

## Notes

Clap parse failures stay outside the envelope and keep writing to stderr. Success-path warnings, such as those `issue create` prints, stay on stderr as documented; this change concerns failure rendering only. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

title: Reduce main.rs to parse, bootstrap, dispatch, render and exit
description:
With every command group handled in the library, `crates/jit/src/main.rs` shrinks to the thin entry the architecture describes and becomes the crate's only process-exit site.

## Background

`main.rs` historically held `run()` (about 6,400 lines), the classifier, about fifteen JSON-error emitters, and about 75 `std::process::exit` calls, which skip `Drop` for the `RetainedMutationSessionGuard` and the `DispatchMutationAnnotation` guard. Command groups now return `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>` from handlers in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`, failures classify through `jit::output::failure::classify`, the output mode is one global flag, and a library function opens the repository and returns the executor with its retained-session guard. Leftovers remain: `writeln_safe` and `writeln_safe_stderr` in the output module call `std::process::exit(ExitCode::BrokenPipe.code())`, `handle_json_error!` in `crates/jit/src/output_macros.rs` expands to an exit, the clap parse failure exits through `error.exit()`, and whatever helper, emitter or storage call no handler migration removed.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `main.rs` contains parsing, one call to the library repository bootstrap, one group dispatch, one rendering of the `Outcome` or failure, and exit; it holds no classifier, JSON-error emitter, macro use or storage call.
- [hard] REQ-02: The crate's production code calls `std::process::exit` from exactly one site, in `main()`; broken-pipe writes and clap parse failures return values that reach it, and parse failures keep clap's diagnostic and exit status.
- [hard] REQ-03: The retained mutation session and the linked-checkout annotation guard are dropped before that exit.
- [hard] REQ-04: `handle_json_error!` no longer exists, and `output_macros.rs` keeps only macros with a remaining use.
- [hard] REQ-05: No function in `main.rs` exceeds 500 lines.
- [hard] REQ-06: A broken stdout pipe still exits with `ExitCode::BrokenPipe`, asserted by a test, and the existing CLI suites pass without weakened assertions.
- [hard] REQ-07: The exit-code projection in `crates/jit/src/schema.rs` describes findings and failures as exiting through the one exit site with the envelope's code, keeps no per-command `std::process::exit` exception, and `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` is regenerated.

## Notes

title: Enforce a main.rs production-line ceiling in the budget script
description:
`scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` gains a fourth budget that caps the production code lines of `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, so the thin entry point cannot regrow.

## Background

The script declares three `readonly` budgets (`MAX_INTEGRATION_TARGETS`, `MAX_EXECUTABLE_BYTES`, `MAX_TEST_SUITE_SECONDS`), accumulates violations in `errors[]`, and on success prints one `rust-build-budget: integration-targets=… suite-duration=…` line. `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` greps `rust-build-budget: integration-targets=.*` and stores the rest in the gate summary. Production lines are defined by the committed counter `scripts/production-lines.py`, which reads files at a git revision. title: Classify document path-read failures by variant
description:
Document path-read failures classify to codes that misdescribe them, so a status derived from the classification would be wrong. This gives each `PathReadError` variant its own code.

## Background

`PathReadError` (`crates/jit/src/storage/path_errors.rs`) has the variants `NotFound`, `CommitNotFound`, `InvalidPath`, `OutsideRepoRoot` and `Other`. The library classifier in `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs` maps `NotFound` and `CommitNotFound` to `REPOSITORY_NOT_FOUND`, labelling a missing document as a missing repository, maps `InvalidPath` to `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and maps `OutsideRepoRoot` to `GENERIC_ERROR` (exit 1). The HTTP server keeps its own map that answers 404 and 400 for these. For the server to derive its status from the classification, the classification itself must name these failures correctly.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `OutsideRepoRoot` classifies to `INVALID_ARGUMENT` as `InvalidPath` already does, and `NotFound` and `CommitNotFound` classify to a document-not-found code in the not-found exit class; `Other` classifies by its inner error as today.
- [hard] REQ-02: The document-not-found code is a member of the error-code vocabulary with a description, and the generated error-code reference lists it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Library unit tests own each variant's classification, and a CLI test states the new code and exit status of `jit doc show` for a missing document and for a path outside the repository.
- [hard] REQ-04: No other error's classification changes, and the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

This is a deliberate, user-visible exit-code change. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

planning.outcome: PathReadError variants classify to INVALID_ARGUMENT or a document-not-found code instead of generic or repository-not-found codes

title: Derive server HTTP statuses from the library classification
description:
The HTTP server stops keeping its own error-to-status mappings and projects the library's failure classification into a status.

## Background

`crates/server/src/routes.rs` handlers return `Result<Json<T>, StatusCode>`. `path_read_error_status` maps `PathReadError` (NotFound/CommitNotFound → 404, InvalidPath/OutsideRepoRoot → 400, Other → 500) for seven document routes, and about eighteen blanket `map_err(|_| StatusCode::…)` sites map any error to 500 (`list_issues`, `get_graph`, `get_status`, `search_issues`, `list_gates`, `get_strategic_types`, `get_hierarchy`, `get_namespaces`) or 404 (`get_issue`, `get_gate_definition`, `list_gate_runs`, `get_gate_run`). These disagree with the CLI: `get_issue` reports an IO failure as 404, and `OutsideRepoRoot` is exit 1 in the CLI but 400 over HTTP. The server already depends on `jit` and can call `jit::output::failure::classify(&anyhow::Error) -> JsonError`; document reads return `Result<_, PathReadError>`, which converts with `anyhow::Error::from`. HTTP types stay out of the `jit` crate.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The server crate holds one function mapping `ErrorCode` to `StatusCode` by an exhaustive `match` with no wildcard arm, so a new code fails to compile until it is mapped.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every route's failure status is that function applied to `classify`'s code for the error; `path_read_error_status` and every blanket `map_err(|_| StatusCode::…)` are gone.
- [hard] REQ-03: Route tests derive expected statuses from the classification of the induced failure, and one owning unit test covers the code-to-status projection.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each route whose status changes for a failure has a test stating the new status, and the remaining server route tests pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

Where the CLI and the server disagreed today, the classification wins. 0f8efc37 REQ-07 later wraps the handlers in one helper that calls this projection. Embedded static-asset 404s are not error classification and are out of scope. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

planning.outcome: Server routes map failures through classify and one exhaustive ErrorCode-to-StatusCode match

title: Crate-private executor kernel
description:
Closes the executor's public surface to its constructors and family facade accessors, making the shared kernel crate-private, so no consumer outside `crates/jit` can bypass a family facade.

## Background

With every family reached through a facade (`CommandExecutor::issues()` returning `IssueOps<'_, S>`, and its peers), the kernel in `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs` is still public: `repository_layout`, `storage`, `rules`, `effective_rules`, `require_active_lease`, and the `pub config_manager: ConfigManager` field. title: Retire error codes that nothing produces
description:
Once every call site classifies failures by type, the `ErrorCode` variants that only fallback sites produced are dead vocabulary and are removed.

## Background

`ErrorCode` in `crates/jit/src/output.rs` declares codes that existed only so a call site could substitute them: candidates include `GateCheckError`, `GateError`, `DependencyError`, `PresetError`, the `Claim*Error` family, the `Worktree*Error` family, `ItemCommandFailed`, `InvariantCommandFailed`, `ProjectCommandFailed`, `HooksInstallError`, `SearchFailed`, `RecoveryFailed` and `ProfileError`. With command groups moved to library handlers whose failures go through `jit::output::failure::classify`, a code is live only if some error type classifies to it or a findings outcome registers it. - [hard] REQ-02: No production code constructs a `JsonError` or exit code from a code chosen at the call site.
- [hard] REQ-03: `docs/reference/error-codes.md` and `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` are regenerated from the reduced vocabulary, and the failure-lever registry names only live codes.

title: Omit clap-hidden commands and flags from the generated schema
description:
The generated command schema stops advertising clap-hidden commands and flags as ordinary surface.

## Background

`CommandSchema::generate()` in `crates/jit/src/schema.rs` walks `Cli::command()` through `extract_command_with_path_hidden` and builds flags with `extract_flag`. Neither consults clap's `Command::is_hide_set` / `Arg::is_hide_set` (clap 4.5). As a result the verb-hint stubs declared `hide = true` in `crates/jit/src/cli.rs` appear as leaves described "Hidden stub: …" with the generic `CommandResponse`, and the hidden `validate --divergence` flag appears in `validate`'s flags. The schema's own `hidden` field is unrelated: `hidden_commands()` marks paths hidden from the default MCP tool listing and must keep working. The MCP server (`mcp-server/lib/tool-generator.js`) turns every schema leaf and flag into tool input, and `mcp-server/curated-tools.json` lists 13 "Alias stub" exclusions that a curation-coverage test in `mcp-server/test-unit.js` checks against the schema.

- [hard] REQ-01: `extract_command_with_path_hidden` skips every subcommand whose `is_hide_set()` is true, and `extract_flag`'s caller skips every argument whose `is_hide_set()` is true.
- [hard] REQ-02: A schema unit test derives the hidden set from `Cli::command()` and asserts none of it appears in the generated schema, and the hidden `validate --divergence` flag is absent.
- [hard] REQ-03: `hidden_commands()` and `builtin_global_flags()` keep their current effect on the schema, and `generate()` remains the schema's derivation authority.
- [hard] REQ-04: The MCP unit and integration tests pass against the reduced schema.

## Notes

The verb-hint stubs themselves are removed separately; this change keeps the schema correct whether or not hidden items exist. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

title: Derive output schemas from the handler registry
description:
The schema's per-command success types come from the handler registry instead of a hand-kept match table, so every visible command names its typed response.

## Background

`get_output_schema_for_command(cmd_path)` in `crates/jit/src/schema.rs` matches `"group_sub"` strings to `schema_for!(T)` and falls back to `(None, "CommandResponse")`. - [hard] REQ-03: A schema test walks the visible executable paths of `Cli::command()` and fails when any has no registered response.
- [hard] REQ-04: Commands whose schema output changes from `CommandResponse` to a typed response, `graph rdeps` among them, are covered by a schema test stating the typed response, and existing schema suites pass without weakened assertions.
- [hard] REQ-05: MCP tool generation and its unit and integration tests pass against the regenerated schema.

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

title: State the CLI output contract once in the command reference

title: Build hygiene and measured completion for crates/jit
description:
The zero-warning bar, the test harness and the size of `main.rs` are enforced by manifests and the budget script rather than by convention, and the epic closes with a measured before/after report.

## Background

Neither workspace manifest declares a `[lints]` table, so `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` without `-D warnings` does not reproduce the gate's bar, and `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` sits on four crate roots only. `crates/jit/tests/common/harness.rs` is `#[path]`-included into four integration targets and recompiles in each. `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` enforces integration-target count, executable bytes and suite duration, but nothing stops `crates/jit/src/main.rs` from regrowing after the dispatch refactor. The survey's production-line figure was not reproducible until the counter `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/prodlines.py` was committed.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Both workspace crate manifests inherit a `[workspace.lints]` table that denies `warnings` and `unsafe_code`, and a bare `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` fails on any warning.
- [hard] REQ-02: The shared integration-test harness is compiled once inside `jit`'s `test-support` surface, and no integration target includes it by `#[path]`.
- [hard] REQ-03: `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` fails when `crates/jit/src/main.rs` exceeds a declared production-code-line ceiling and reports the measured value on its existing `rust-build-budget:` success line.
- [hard] REQ-04: A committed completion report records production code lines for `crates/jit/src` per top-level module before and after the epic, counted by one committed counter, together with the re-measured integration-target and executable-byte budgets.

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

planning.outcome: Lints live in the manifests, the harness compiles once, main.rs has a ceiling, and line counts are reported before and after

title: One library error boundary for the CLI and the server
description:
Failures in `crates/jit` are classified once, in the library, by error type, and both the CLI and the HTTP server project that one classification into their own surface.

## Background

The classifier `error_to_error_code` and its exit-code projection live in `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, where the server cannot reach them. Around it, `main.rs` holds at least fifteen parallel JSON-error emitters (`command_json_error`, `claim_json_error`, `profile_json_error`, `gate_pass_json_error`, `dep_add_batch_json_error`, `handle_json_error!` and others) and more than fifty call sites that substitute their own fallback code, so the human and `--json` paths can exit with different codes for the same error. `std::process::exit` is called about 75 times, which skips `Drop` for the retained mutation session. `main()` prints an `Error:` line to stderr even when it also prints the `--json` envelope. `crates/server/src/routes.rs` keeps its own `path_read_error_status` map and blanket `map_err(|_| StatusCode::…)` conversions that disagree with the CLI.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One library function, `jit::output::failure::classify`, derives each error's code, message, details and suggestions from the error's type, and `crates/jit/src/main.rs` contains no classifier, per-command JSON-error helper or error macro.
- [hard] REQ-02: No call site substitutes an error code, the human and `--json` paths exit with the same code for the same error, and `ErrorCode` declares no code that nothing produces.
- [hard] REQ-03: Once clap has accepted the arguments, under `--json` a failing invocation writes one envelope to stdout and nothing to stderr; in human mode it writes one `Error:` diagnostic to stderr.
- [hard] REQ-04: `main()` is parse, bootstrap, dispatch, render and exit, and the crate's production code calls `std::process::exit` from that one site.
- [hard] REQ-05: The server derives every failure's HTTP status from the library classification through one exhaustive code-to-status projection.
- [hard] REQ-06: Each deliberate change to an exit code, error code, stderr content or HTTP status has a test stating the new contract, and the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

planning.outcome: One library classifier owns every failure's code, exit code, details and HTTP status, and main.rs holds the only exit

title: One stated output and schema contract for the CLI
description:
The CLI's machine and human output are produced by shared types and renderers in the output module, the generated schema derives from them, and the contract is stated once in the reference docs.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/output.rs` declares 33 hand-written `count` structs, eight of which (`ReadyQueryResponse` … `ClosedQueryResponse`) are dead, while `ProfileCollection<T>` in `profile/application.rs` is already a generic envelope with a fixed key. `CommandSchema::generate()` in `crates/jit/src/schema.rs` types output through the hand table in `get_output_schema_for_command`, which falls back to `CommandResponse` for 74 of 120 leaves and lists clap-hidden stubs and the hidden `validate --divergence` flag as ordinary surface. Human rendering of the issue list, the validation report, gate run status and archive execution is copied across dispatch arms in several diverging forms. The list envelope is stated only in `README.md` and `docs/concepts/design-philosophy.md`, and `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` documents behaviour this epic changes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every list payload is an instantiation of one generic `ListEnvelope` type in the output module, no hand-written `count` struct remains, and each command keeps the `{"count": N, "<collection>": [...]}` wire shape.
- [hard] REQ-02: The generated schema omits everything clap marks hidden and names a registered, typed success response for every visible executable command, with no hand-kept path-to-type table.
- [hard] REQ-03: The issue list, validation report, gate run status and archive execution views each have one renderer in the output module that every printing command calls.
- [hard] REQ-04: `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` states the list envelope, the global `--json`, the one-rendering-per-invocation stream rule, the findings envelope and the wrong-verb hint behaviour once, and other pages cite it.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each deliberate change to human output, schema names or schema content has a test stating the new contract, and the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.

planning.outcome: List payloads share one envelope type, shared human views have one renderer, and the schema derives every leaf's type

title: Library-side command dispatch for crates/jit
description:
Moves command dispatch out of the 6,400-line `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` into library-side handlers that return typed command or domain results and failures as values, on top of one global `--json` flag and one shared issue-filter argument group.

## Background

`run()` matches over the 29 `Commands` variants and builds success payloads, chooses error codes, prints and calls `std::process::exit` inside the arms. `cli.rs` declares 108 per-command `json` fields, `main.rs` scans raw argv for `--json` twice, 13 hidden verb stubs shadow the parser-level hint path, issue filters are parsed at about 14 sites, and 74 of 120 schema leaves fall back to `CommandResponse`. Several arms reach `storage`, `jit::search`, the claims free functions and the serve process helpers directly instead of the executor or `commands/`.

On main, `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` parses the arguments and calls `dispatch()` in `main.rs`, which holds the command match; the arms and inline code this issue places in `run()` live in `dispatch()`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `--json` is one global flag carried as `OutputMode`; no subcommand declares a `json` field, no code reads raw argv for it.
- [hard] REQ-02: No hidden verb-hint stub remains; a wrong verb prints its hint and clap's diagnostic on stderr and exits 2, with or without `--json`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every issue-filtering command takes its filters from one flattened `IssueFilterArgs` group parsed once at the CLI boundary.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every command group dispatches from `run()` to a handler in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`, and every visible schema leaf names the typed command or domain result its handler returns.
- [hard] REQ-05: Handlers return failures and findings as values: no handler substitutes a fallback code for an ordinary error, prints an error envelope or calls `std::process::exit`; declared findings use the shared outcome/emitter, and worktree execution retains child-status passthrough (exit 1 when no numeric status exists), while foreground serve remains a typed failure, and each deliberate exit-code, envelope or schema change has a test stating the new contract.
- [hard] REQ-06: The migrated handlers make no storage, `jit::search`, claims free-function or serve process call; they go through the executor or `commands/`.

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.
## Decisions

- D-01: Reconcile response ownership with the user-approved epic REQ-01 and plan D-59: command or domain results are rendered and enveloped by output, without a command-to-output dependency.

- D-02: Reconcile REQ-05 with the accepted findings protocol (plan D-42) and the 0eca332a D-02 boundary correction. The steward approved the existing findings and worktree child-status behavior on 2026-11-04; ordinary errors still require canonical typed classification, with no new arbitrary-code sites or behavior change.

planning.outcome: Every command group dispatches from a thin run() to a typed library handler over one global --json and shared filter args

title: Narrow executor surface and storage-free CLI entry
description:
Splits the monolithic `CommandExecutor` public surface into per-family facades and moves every storage call, repository bootstrap, search, claim and foreground-serve step the CLI makes on its own behind the executor or `commands/`.

## Background

`CommandExecutor` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`) exposes about 195 methods in 28 `impl` blocks across 25 files, so any consumer that needs one family (the HTTP server needs issues, documents, gates and validation) accepts the whole surface, including session and cache internals and a `pub config_manager` field. Separately, `crates/jit/src/main.rs` bypasses the executor: `run()` constructs `JsonFileStorage`, opens mutation sessions and calls `storage.validate()`; issue arms call `storage.resolve_issue_id` and `storage.load_issue` after each mutation; `Commands::Search` calls `jit::search::search`; claim and recover arms call `commands::claim` free functions with `&storage`; and foreground `jit serve` spawns and waits on the server inline and calls `std::process::exit`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each command family is reachable through a facade returned by a `CommandExecutor` accessor (for example `issues()` returning `IssueOps<'_, S>`), and the executor's public surface is limited to its constructors and those accessors.
- [hard] REQ-02: The CLI command path makes no direct `IssueStore` or `JsonFileStorage` call: repository opening, issue mutations, template application, search, claims and foreground serve go through library functions that return what the CLI reports.
- [hard] REQ-03: The CLI's human output, JSON output and exit codes are unchanged by this restructuring, and the existing Rust suites pass with no assertion weakened.

## Notes

- 0f8efc37 later adopts the repository bootstrap for the server and replaces what the executor search entry point computes.
- Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md` (D-1, D-11); method inventory: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md` area 3.

planning.outcome: CommandExecutor is reached through per-family facades, and the CLI path makes no direct storage or library-bypass call.
